messages:
mike: FYI after the overnight kernel rollout we see a perf regression on Mixtral MoE small-batch traces — p95 throughput down ~8% on short conversations.
sara: noticed similar on LLM-test-suite, p99 spikes too. looked like a tail regression not average.
infra-bot: deploy bot: rolled runtime-kernel v3.9.1 -> all regions; changed config: eager_kernel_switch = true :white_check_mark:
yoshi: digging through runtime logs: kernel-selection is oscillating for small batches. per-request kernel switch latency ~200-400µs in hot path.
```
select_kernel(batch=2, seq=32) -> kernel_q8_fast
launch -> kernel_q8_small
select_kernel(batch=2, seq=64) -> kernel_dense_long
```
this flip-flop is happening mid-sequence for many requests.
profiling-bot: sampled perf (mixtral-moex, 8xA100): baseline (v3.8.0) mean per-token GPU time=1.85ms; v3.9.1 w/ eager switch=1.92ms. kernel switch overhead ~+0.35ms each. KV-cache eviction rate spikes correlated with router reassignment events.
manual: collected 10k-request canary: kernel_switch_count per-req median=0, 95p=3 for small batches. eviction_count 95p +2.8x vs baseline.
anya: hypothesis: eager_kernel_switch aims to pick optimal kernel for current sequence length and quant profile; for MoE the router's varying top-k causes backend paths to vary (quantized experts vs dense experts), leading to kernel churn and repeated KV cache reshuffles (evictions and reloads).
sara: mitigation ideas:
- sticky-kernel: bind a sequence id to a chosen kernel for N tokens (N ~ 128) to avoid thrash
- topk-stability window: only allow kernel switch after T consecutive top-k stability ticks
- batch-aware threshold: disallow switch when batch_size <= B
- prefer delayed switch (defer switch until next batch boundary)
mike: pragmatic plan: flip eager_kernel_switch off for mixtral-moex in canary pool; run short-convo and long-context scenarios; collect kernel_switch_count, p95, evictions; then try sticky-kernel on canary.
anya: I'll draft a lightweight sticky-kernel patch: feature flag sticky_kernel.enabled=false by default; params: sticky_tokens=128, stability_window=3. will post PR shortly.
yoshi: I can toggle config quickly. curl example:
```
curl -X POST "https://runtime.internal/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"mixtral-moex","eager_kernel_switch":false}'
```
(should propagate in ~30s)
infra-bot: applied config change to canary at 2311122360 :white_check_mark:
profiling-bot: canary run (10k requests) results: kernel_switch_count 95p -> down from 3 to 0; p95 latency improved 6.3% on short flows; KV-eviction-rate -42% vs v3.9.1; GPU utilization steady.
mike: solid. hold full rollout. we need sticky-kernel patch + perf test across other moex variants (mixtral-large, mixtral-xl) before re-enabling eager switch globally.
anya: PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4824 (draft) — adds sticky-kernel + stability_window. small unit tests included.
yoshi: monitoring router hotkeys now; will post traces. trace id trace-2311122334-01.
profiling-bot: note — some workloads with long open conversations (seq > 2048) still benefit from kernel switch. sticky-kernel should be tunable per-model + per-workload.
mike: next steps: (1) merge sticky-kernel with default off (2) run canary with sticky enabled for mixtral-moex and tune sticky_tokens/stability_window (3) add model-opt-in map so moex models default to sticky off until we validate (4) update rollout PR to gate eager switch behind model opt-in.
sara: will add regression test to LLM-test-suite to catch kernel churn + KV-eviction spikes in CI.
anya: will include telemetry counters: kernel_switch_count, switch_latency_hist, sticky_bind_hits, topk_stability_metric, kv_eviction_count.
yoshi: will create dashboard widgets for these metrics per-model and per-region.
mike: thanks team. good catch on canary. :thumbsup:
